newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Profit seen for Hanbo steel from 2001.
newsitem.headline: Profit seen for Hanbo steel from 2001.

text.p: South Korea's financially stricken Hanbo Steel Co Ltd is forecast to post a profit from the year 2001, a court appointed management team for the steelmaker said on Wednesday.
The team gave no figures for the profit forecast.
A statement released from the team said Hanbo Steel was expected to pay back its huge debts by 2010.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of the country's 14th largest conglomerate, was declared insolvent in January after piling up $5.8 billion in debts.

The management team, in a meeting with creditors and possible buyers of Hanbo Steel, added that a total of 4.98 trillion won was needed to build the company's new electric-arc furnace steel mill at Tangjin.
It said Hanbo Steel would fully operate its plants for hot-rolled steel and steel rods to make a profit from 2001.
The company posted 64.1 billion won in sales last month, its highest monthly turnover.
Hanbo Steel is forecast to record sales of 1.26 trillion won in 1998 and 2.31 trillion won by 2010. Further details were not given.
South Korea's large conglomerates, including LG Group and Ssangyong Group, participated in the meeting.
